title: The Trolley Problem
summary: A runaway trolley is heading for five people. You can pull a lever to send it onto a side track, where it will kill one person instead. Philippa Foot introduced the case in 1967 (in her version you are the driver); Judith Jarvis Thomson made the one at the lever a bystander, and turned it into one of the most famous puzzles in ethics: why does diverting the trolley seem permissible, when so many other ways of killing one to save five (pushing someone off a footbridge, a surgeon harvesting organs) do not? Answers draw on the difference between doing and allowing harm, and between harming as a side effect and harming as a means. In 2008 Thomson changed her mind, and argued that a bystander may not turn the trolley after all.
